units.function: Large embedded-Postgres authorization decision suite covering user/Agent grants, Company boundaries, responsible-human ceilings, Agent/skill changes, task assignment, issue visibility and mutation, low-trust review boundaries, protected/private Agents, mention-derived access, instance administration, scoped runtime tokens, inbox delegation and Secret proposals.
units.dependencyDirection: Authenticated actor, action, typed resource and optional scope enter AuthorizationService; it reads Company memberships, explicit Principal grants, Agent permission-policy JSON, hierarchy, Issues/comments, instance roles and inbox policy, then emits a structured allow/deny decision with reason, code, explanation and optional matching grant. Routes and services consume that decision before mutation.
units.keyDataModels: Human/Agent Principal, Company membership and role, PermissionKey grant with JSON scope, responsible-user delegation, action/resource/scope tuple, Agent trustPreset/authorizationPolicy/visibility/assignment policy/hierarchy, Issue/project/assignee/origin/comment mention, task_bridge and skill_test key scopes, instance admin, inbox Agent policy and structured decision reason/code.
units.lifecycle: Cross-Company Agent access is denied first. Low-trust boundaries precede explicit change grants and constrain projects, root/child Issues and allowed Agents. Direct grants or consented suggest grants authorize configuration changes; protected/private targets add hard blocks or scoped grants. Standard-trust same-Company Agents receive default-open visible Issue writes and assignment, while active board members receive several null-mapped actions without explicit grants. Mention comments can dynamically grant Issue read/comment. Scoped JWTs constrain task bridges and skill tests. Responsible-human membership/grants cap delegated Agent actions, and per-user inbox policy controls self or cross-user inbox management.
units.testAssessment: More than fifty database-backed cases exercise a broad decision matrix, real SQL filtering, boundary precedence, structured reasons, low-trust containment, cross-Company denial and scope variants; this is one of Paperclip's strongest test assets. Major gaps remain: grant expiry/revocation/version and concurrent runs, deny grants and policy conflict ordering, immutable consent/approval evidence, purpose/data/tool/export conditions, organization position and accountable role, time/network/environment attributes, exhaustive action-resource coverage, property-level mutation, decision audit receipts, performance/query plans and generated completeness checks. Some tests codify fail-open compatibility rather than safe policy.
units.designRationale: Evolve from a simple same-Company collaborative board toward granular governance without breaking existing Agent workflows: keep default-open collaboration and legacy CEO/member behavior, layer explicit grants and scoped tokens, then introduce low-trust presets and responsible-user ceilings as hard constraints.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a single explainable policy decision point for mixed humans and Agents, but authority must derive from organization responsibility, explicit grants, approved actions and data contracts rather than product-era compatibility defaults.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT the policy core while ADAPTing the typed action/resource decision envelope, structured reason/code, explicit scope tests, low-trust precedence, responsible-human ceiling and capability-limited token concepts. Use versioned deny-by-default policy with validated scope schemas, explicit action/resource registry, Principal/Position/ResponsibilityContract, Work/action digest, permission and data grants, risk/approval/evidence context, expiry/revocation and immutable decision receipt. Generate matrix completeness tests and tenant-scope queries.
units.responsibilityConflict: Several intentional defaults violate Company OS invariants: standard-trust Agents may comment on and mutate peer-owned visible Issues without grants; an active non-viewer board member can receive runtime:manage and secrets:read through simple membership; unknown grant-scope metadata is treated as unconstrained; legacy CEO Agents can create Agents without explicit authority; and mutable comment mentions mint access. Responsible-human checks often prove only membership/non-viewer status, not responsibility for the exact action, data or outcome.
